title: RCStat: A Statistical Framework for using Relative Contextualization in Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2506.19549v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Identifying which tokens and activations truly influence model predictions is critical for both the efficiency and interpretability of large auto-regressive language models. Yet in practice, token importance is typically inferred from attention distributions that entangle contextual relevance with softmax-normalization effects, obscuring relative influence across tokens and heads. We propose $\textbf{RCStat}$, a statistical framework for quantifying contextual influence in attention mechanisms. At its core $\textbf{Relative Contextualization (RC)}$ is a random variable that measures how strongly one subset of tokens contributes to another under the model's internal scoring scheme. RCStat admits computationally efficient bounds on expected influence that can be estimated at inference time. No retraining is required. We apply RCStat to two tasks. translated_title: RCStat：一种在Transformer中使用相对上下文化的统计框架
translated_abstract: 确定哪些标记（token）和激活真正影响模型预测，对大型自回归语言模型的效率和可解释性都至关重要。然而在实践中，标记的重要性通常是从注意力分布中推断出来的，而这些分布将上下文相关性与softmax归一化效应纠缠在一起，掩盖了不同标记和注意力头之间的相对影响力。我们提出了RCStat，一个用于量化注意力机制中上下文影响力的统计框架。其核心是相对上下文化（Relative Contextualization, RC），它是一个随机变量，用于衡量在模型内部评分方案下，一个标记子集对另一个标记子集的贡献强度。RCStat提供了计算高效的期望影响力边界，可以在推理时进行估计，无需重新训练。我们将RCStat应用于两个任务：在归因任务中，具有高期望RC的注意力头能够准确识别……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出RCStat统计框架，将相对上下文化（RC）建模为随机变量以量化Transformer注意力机制中标记间的真实上下文影响力，无需重新训练即可在推理时高效估计期望影响力，可用于归因等任务。
en_tdlr: RCStat is a statistical framework that models Relative Contextualization (RC) as a random variable to quantify true token influence in attention mechanisms, providing computationally efficient bounds on expected influence at inference time without retraining.
